messages.content: Your response must include bullet points denoted by * and at least one sub-bullet point denoted by - for each bullet point. Ensure that stop words constitute no more than 27% of the total words in your response. Write a fictional, imaginative, descriptive timeline of an alternate universe where the new world was only discovered in the 1900s with the advent of satellites

message.content:
* 1903 — Orbital telescopes mounted atop Kármán line capture first grainy images of vast landmass beneath Pacific fog bank.
  - Astronomers initially dismiss photographs as atmospheric refraction anomalies, yet three independent stations confirm dense green terrain stretching thousands of miles.

* 1911 — "Verdant Discovery" erupts in global headlines as satellite arrays reveal coastlines, rivers, sprawling forests never charted by terrestrial expedition.
  - Governments scramble to classify images; military satellites shift orbits to prevent rival nations from obtaining superior resolution data.

* 1924 — First intercontinental relay satellites beam live footage of indigenous settlements nestled in river valleys, shattering assumption that landmass remained uninhabited.
  - Philosophers, theologians convene in Geneva, debating whether centuries of recorded human history require radical revision.

* 1937 — Joint Anglo-French orbital platform deploys first high-altitude survey drones, mapping mountain ranges, coastal cities, ancient stone monuments predating European civilizations by millennia.
  - Archaeologists weep openly before imagery, recognizing architectural patterns echoing Sumerian, Mesoamerican design simultaneously.

* 1949 — Post-war satellite constellations orbit ceaselessly, broadcasting continuous video feeds revealing seasonal migrations, agricultural cycles, complex trade networks across newly visible continent.
  - Radio broadcasts of ambient sounds—birdsong, market chatter, river currents—reach living rooms worldwide, igniting cultural renaissance of cartography, ethnography.

* 1963 — "Aerial Contact Accord" establishes protocols: no ground incursions permitted until orbital observation periods span at least three decades.
  - Satellite operators maintain respectful distances; zooming above cloud cover to study atmospheric chemistry becomes standard scientific practice rather than colonial reconnaissance.

* 1981 — Resolution advances to point where individual faces become distinguishable during dawn ceremonies along western shore.
  - Ethics boards halt all magnification beyond 400x, declaring that further visual intimacy crosses moral boundary no technology should breach.

* 2003 — Two centuries of patient orbital watching conclude; landmass's inhabitants have, in several remote valleys, begun building crude metallic spheres, attempting to reach glowing objects circling overhead.
  - Cycle inverts: observers become observed, true discovery belongs now to those gazing upward.
